content: {"english": "Today too we are going to study types of machine learning, but the types we will discuss today will be based on a completely different thing, so the types of machine learning we are going to study depend on how the machine learning model is trained, especially in production. Now you might think what is production? So let me first define what is production in simpler terms. Production is basically the server on which your code is going to run. Whenever you build any software,"}

{"english": "So it should not stay on your machine, it should go to your customers, and there is only one way, that you run your code on a server whose IP address will be with your customers, they will hit that IP address and will be able to access your application. Machine learning is more different, when you build machine learning software, you also deploy it on a server, and the server environment where your code is running, that is called the production environment, when you are coding it"}

{"english": "Because at the end you will not keep the machine learning models you build on your own machine, you will deploy it on a server so that other people can use it, so you should have an idea of what the difference is between batch and online learning, so that's the intro part, now let's discuss what batch learning is, what is batch learning? Batch learning is the conventional way of training a machine learning model where you what you do is you take the entire data all at once."}

{"english": "no doubt you can do it, but no one does it because it would be costly and time-taking generally, where batch learning happens, where you are training with the entire data all at once, you do it offline on your machine, the data scientist, machine learning engineer trains it on their machine, and when that model is trained, you take the learned model and put it in the production environment, this is called batch learning where you take up your entire data, you train your machine learning model on an offline system."}

{"english": "and then once the model is trained then you deploy it onto a server this is the entire flow of batch learning I'll draw it for you so what happens it is very simple you have data this is your data and this is your model right you put your data on the model the model gets trained after training you test the model just be sure that what I have trained is correct or not"}

{"english": "once you are sure you put it on the server this is the server okay and over there your machine learning model will keep running whenever the user gives any data your machine learning model will keep making predictions it could be anything let's say you work at Netflix and you want to implement a recommendation engine that tells users which movie to select okay so in that case what will you do you will train that recommendation engine on your machine and you will take it and put it on the Netflix server where"}

{"english": "when users come, your system will automatically keep suggesting movies to them, right? But I guess you are understanding a problem in this thing. The problem with this thing is that your model is static. Once it learns, it has learned; it is not learning anything new. After that, it is working only on the old things. But the problem with this approach is that your business scenario keeps evolving. I'll give you one example. We are talking about Netflix. Netflix's recommendation engine."}

{"english": "What you made, let's say if you made it today, considering all the movies that were in Netflix's database today, but Netflix keeps adding new movies every week, so your recommendation engine should always grow in order to incorporate those new movies, right? So in a way, what I am saying is that your machine learning model has to constantly evolve with the data, because if you don't do that, then what is the use? Your recommendation won't work on new movies. The same thing can happen in the email spam classifier. Your email spam classifier from today's date"}

{"english": "It is completely up to date with today's date, but after you put it on the server, no training was done. You left it for a year, but in that one year, the marketers will come up with new techniques to make spam emails, you know, in the spam folder. So if you don't keep your system up to date, then what's the point? It will become obsolete. So the biggest problem with batch learning is that you have to keep retraining your model. So what you do is generally people do what"}

{"english": "they do this entire thing periodically so what they do is that they bring new data, this data is being updated all the time, it is being updated, it can be updated at any frequency, it can be updated in 24 hours or in one week or in one month. Your job is that as this data is being updated, what are you doing, you are merging all the new data and the old data and then training the model again, once the model is trained"}

{"english": "You are testing it again and after testing, you are putting it on the server again, so basically this whole process happens in circles, it keeps repeating over and over in a given period, this could be a 24 hour period, this could be a week period or a month period or a six months period. Generally, people want to do this very fast, but it depends how fast it is, it depends on the amount of data, like if you have a huge amount of data, then even in training"}

{"english": "it will take time, so generally people do it on a basis of per week or then 24 hours, but yeah that is what batch learning is. I am summarizing batch learning once. Batch learning is where you train your machine learning model with your entire data. There is no incremental learning, and that is why since generally the data is big, you don't train it online on the server. Instead, what you do is you pull down your model, you retrain it with the new data, and then you put it on the server again and again."}

{"english": "You do this periodically, okay? So that is what batch learning is now. If someone asks you what the disadvantage of batch learning is, then the first disadvantage is that if you have a lot of data, the data keeps getting very big, you are scaling very fast. You are a social network that is doubling, tripling, four times every month or two months, so the amount of data is also increasing a lot. So if your data becomes very big, it is also possible that your existing tools, which are to handle that much data,"}

{"english": "you can't process it, right? Your data has converted into big data, so you are not able to give the whole chunks at once. Your code is not fitting, right? So that is one problem, that since you have a limitation that it will train with the whole data, so if the whole data becomes very big, then it won't be able to train, right? The second problem is hardware limitation. What is hardware limitation? It is that sometimes it might be that your machine learning model is running in a place where you do not have instant connectivity, so you cannot do that."}

{"english": "that you bring the model from Trend and train it on new data, then upload it. You don't have this facility. I give you one or two scenarios. Let's say you made a defense app that the army people are using. In an extremely extreme scenario, in a battlefield-like place, those people are using your machine learning app to track something or to do something. Now there is no internet access there, so your model is running on their phone as an app."}

{"english": "So once it has gone, until those people come back or come into an internet connectivity zone, you cannot pull it down and train and update it, so that is a limitation, right? Similarly, let's say you have built a machine learning software that you want to send to a satellite. Now, once the satellite goes into orbit, who knows if there is internet connectivity there or if you have put it in a drone, that drone is not known which place it is picking up from, so in such scenarios where you do not have connectivity to talk to your model"}

{"english": "So if you cannot take such frequent updates, then batch learning fails in such places, it fails. Third is availability. I told you, what do you generally do? You update your model with new data in a 24-hour period, right? But there is a problem in this too. Let's say you are working on a social networking website and you have built a model that brings and shows the most recent stories. Sorry, your social networking website generates the news feed"}

{"english": "it does on the basis of user's interest, right? But here you have put batch learning, so it updates only after 24 hours on the new data. Now, something sudden, something suddenly, anything can happen on your network. If the Indian government has some news about demonetization, then this is a news about which everyone will be interested, I will also be interested, someone else will be interested, although my preference is generally sports, but still since demonetization is affecting me too, so I am interested in it."}

{"english": "but when will my interest updates be, think about it, after 24 hours, right, I am clicking on such news, I am clicking on the demonetization news feed by myself, so when will my update be, after 24 hours, because when did I generate new data, just now, but I want the demonetization news instantly in my news feed, right, but I cannot get it because my system itself will respond only after 24 hours, so in this scenario, what is the problem is that when the system updates after 24 hours, my news feed will suddenly be completely filled"}

{"english": "The news of demonetization, which was so important 24 hours ago, is not that important now either. So in this scenario, you can see how batch learning is failing. Okay, so most people use batch learning in many scenarios, but there are certain specific scenarios where batch learning is not helpful. Okay, it actually creates a problem. So in such scenarios, another approach is used, which we call online learning, which we will discuss next."}
